Confirmed — only `src/lib/errors.ts` has the exhaustive `Record<ErrorCode, ...>` mapping that the compiler forces to stay complete. Now compiling the final list.

**Source files:**
- `src/types/api.ts` — add the new literal to the `ErrorCode` union itself.
- `src/lib/errors.ts` — extend `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` (a `Record<ErrorCode, number>`, so this won't compile without the new key) and, if a new domain error class maps to it, `toAppError()`.

**Documents that enumerate the full closed union and would go stale:**
- `docs/adr/ADR-014-domain-errors-to-error-codes.md` — states "exactly nine codes" and lists them all.
- `docs/design/action-wrapper-and-errors.md` — DES-222's table lists every code/class/status mapping.
- `docs/design/data-flow.md` — DES-025 spells out the full `ErrorCode` enumeration in prose.
- `docs/api/actions-overview.md` — repeats "the nine `ErrorCode` values and their status codes."
- `docs/glossary.md` — the "Error code" glossary entry lists all nine values explicitly.

Files like `docs/design/permission-model.md`, `docs/traceability.md`, and `scripts/manifest-parts/lib.ts` reference `ErrorCode` but don't enumerate its members, so they don't need edits; the two `.code === "plan_limit_exceeded"` checks in `invite-accept-form.tsx`/`webhook-manager.tsx` are single-value comparisons, not exhaustive switches, so they're unaffected too.

ANSWER: src/types/api.ts, src/lib/errors.ts, docs/adr/ADR-014-domain-errors-to-error-codes.md, docs/design/action-wrapper-and-errors.md, docs/design/data-flow.md, docs/api/actions-overview.md, docs/glossary.md
